flagged.evidence: The paragraph requires injectivity “so that each spatial slice is an embedded sheet”, although singleton times explicitly have no rank condition. Take D=[-1,1]^2, I={0}, r(u,v,0)=(u^2,u^3,v), its constant-in-time polynomial extension, and ambient fields v=0 and B=0. These satisfy every standing hypothesis and the additional injectivity requirement. Nevertheless the image has a cuspidal ridge and is not a C1 embedded surface near the origin. Normalized secants along (u^2,u^3,0) converge to e1, so an embedded surface would have e1 tangent and admit a two-sided C1 curve through the origin with derivative e1. This is impossible because the first coordinate is nonnegative throughout the image and therefore has derivative zero along every such curve at the origin. Injectivity alone does not supply the asserted differential embedding at the admitted singleton slices.
